The test image shows a mango leaf with scattered dark/black spots across its surface, on a pale background. The leaf has a greenish-gray color with multiple small black spots distributed across it.

Key observations:
- Dark black spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Leaf appears somewhat discolored/mottled green-gray
- No obvious powdery white coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No wilting/curling pattern typical of Die_Back
- Could be Anthracnose (dark spots) or Sooty_Mould (black encrustations)

Let me view one reference image for Sooty_Mould since the pattern looks most like black surface encrustations.

The Sooty_Mould reference image is nearly identical to the test image:
- Same mottled green-gray leaf with scattered black spots/encrustations
- Same pattern of dark deposits across the leaf surface
- Same pale background and photographic style

This is a very strong match. The black spots are superficial encrustations consistent with sooty mould (fungal mycelium growing on honeydew), not the sunken/lesion-type spots of Anthracnose.
